name: Campobaja
description: A two-floor Roma Norte restaurant built on the cooking of a Mexican fish camp, with a shareable menu of ceviches, aguachiles, tostadas and fish tacos. There is no fixed menu; it depends on the day's catch from Veracruz and Baja California. Fried spiny lobster and grilled octopus come up repeatedly. It carries a Michelin Guide listing.
special_quality: A Michelin-listed fish-camp kitchen whose menu changes with the daily catch.
google_maps_query: Campobaja, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Aguachile en la CDMX

name: Ultramarinos Demar
subcategory: Seafood bistro, raw bar and pastas
description: A corner diner-meets-bistro in stainless steel, with an open kitchen fronted by a counter with stools. Chef Lucho Martinez cooks seafood in a raw section, pastas, mains and daily specials. Michelin lists it as a Bib Gourmand.
special_quality: A Bib Gourmand counter-seat seafood bistro that treats fish like a Mediterranean-Mexican deli.
google_maps_query: Ultramarinos Demar, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Mariscos Don Vergas
description: Chef Luis Valle's Sinaloa-style seafood spot began as a stall in Mercado de San Juan and now has its own storefront on Río Lerma. The Infatuation singles out the tostada embarazada loaded with shrimp, octopus, crab, fish and scallops. Other picks are aguachile, pescado zarandeado, octopus chicharrón tacos and the taco gobernador. It is one of the pricier marisquerías.
special_quality: The market stall that became a Sinaloa-shack-quality destination, home of the tostada embarazada.
google_maps_query: Mariscos Don Vergas, Cuauhtémoc, Ciudad de Mexico

name: La Guerrerense (Condesa)
description: The Mexico City branch of Sabina Bandera's Ensenada street cart, which her in-laws opened in 1960 and which Bourdain made famous. The tostadas are the draw: paté de pescado, caracol, and the Singapur of crab salad with shrimp, octopus and scallop. Chilango calls them unique in Ensenada, in CDMX and in the country. Ask which salsa goes with which tostada.
special_quality: Ensenada's famous street-cart tostadas, with the salsas, served in Condesa.
google_maps_query: La Guerrerense, Condesa, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Tasting Table - Bourdain and the world's best tostadas

name: Henry Sailor
description: A corner of Guaymas in Narvarte, serving tacos, aguachiles and tostadas with craft beer. Chilango points to the tostada embarazada (shrimp, octopus, crab), red tuna and marlin. Time Out highlights the tostada Guaymas, sheets of raw tuna cured in house sauce with crispy onions. Pibil-style fish is also on the menu.
special_quality: Guaymas-style raw tuna tostadas in a craft-beer setting.
google_maps_query: Henry Sailor, Narvarte, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - tostadas de atún

name: Avenida La Tizona
description: Run by two owners from Los Mochis, Sinaloa, who opened in 2018. The menu is traditional rather than reinterpreted: aguachile Juanito with three salsas, and La Negrita, a tostada with peanut mole, octopus and raw shrimp. Weekends bring callo de hacha, oysters and clams, with micheladas. Time Out rates it 3/5.
special_quality: Unreconstructed Los Mochis cart seafood with a peanut-mole tostada.
google_maps_query: Avenida La Tizona, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Avenida La Tizona
Food and Pleasure - Avenida La Tizona

name: La Matoza
description: A family marisquería from Alvarado, Veracruz, described by Chilango as in business since the 1980s and by another list as a 60-year tradition in eastern CDMX. Known for pulpo enamorado, oysters, manitas de jaiba, pescadillas, crab and fish quesadillas and a vuelve a la vida cocktail. Praised for fresh product and friendly service.
special_quality: A Veracruzano family institution of eastern CDMX, known for pulpo enamorado and crab claws.
address: Prolongación Eje 6 Sur 560 (near La Nueva Viga), San José Aculco, Iztapalapa
google_maps_query: La Matoza, Prolongación Eje 6 Sur 560, Ciudad de Mexico

name: El K-Guamo (Mariscos El Caguamo)
description: A Centro street stall with about 40 years of history, serving tostadas of octopus, crab ceviche, fish ceviche and shrimp. One Chilango writer prefers it to the nearby sit-down locale for its attentive service. Very cheap.
special_quality: A roughly 40-year-old Centro stand for pulpo and jaiba tostadas.
google_maps_query: Mariscos El K-Guamo, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Agua y Sal
description: A Polanco cebichería built around ceviches that draw on coastal traditions across Latin America, with Ismael Sánchez as chef. Time Out lists its aguachile with chiltepín, black pepper and fresh shrimp. It has been around since at least 2014 and has about 1,000 OpenTable reviews averaging 4.7.
special_quality: Polanco's long-running pan-Latin cebichería, a serious ceviche menu in a polished room.
google_maps_query: Agua y Sal, Polanco, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Eating the World - Agua y Sal
Time Out México - Aguachile en la CDMX
Food and Pleasure - ceviches frescos en CDMX

name: La Pinguina
description: A seafood corner in central Coyoacán with a Baja California Sur-inspired menu and a conscious-fishing ethos. Time Out gives it 4/5 for the Baja-style shrimp taco, the aguachile negro with roasted habanero and the catch of the day al mojo de ajo. A free cup of shrimp broth arrives on sitting down, and licuachelas come in refillable cups.
special_quality: Baja-style shrimp tacos and aguachile negro in Coyoacán, with a free shrimp broth.
google_maps_query: La Pinguina, Del Carmen, Coyoacán, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Aguachile en la CDMX

name: Tostadas Coyoacán
description: A classic stand in Mercado de Coyoacán with tostadas of cod, ceviche, octopus, pata de mula and shrimp. Every tostada gets a guacamole base and the salsas are fierce. It draws tourists as well as locals.
special_quality: Guacamole-based seafood tostadas at the Coyoacán market, with very hot salsas.
address: Mercado de Coyoacán, Ignacio Allende 49, Coyoacán
google_maps_query: Tostadas Coyoacán, Mercado de Coyoacán, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Taco de Mar
description: A small, unassuming seafood spot that Chilango rates among the city's best. It has a varied menu; the shrimp aguachile is the pick, plus a caldo de camarón for hangovers, and pulpo al pastor and octopus tortas. A second branch is in Del Valle Norte.
special_quality: Unfussy aguachile and pulpo al pastor from a neighborhood seafood taquería.
address: División del Norte 2629, Del Carmen, Coyoacán
google_maps_query: Taco de Mar, Coyoacán, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Mariscos del Diego
description: Praised for ceviches with well-balanced acid and heat and for generous portions. The campechano (shrimp and octopus), seafood pasta and mojarra are the dishes to order. The mojarra takes a while to cook.
special_quality: Big, well-balanced ceviche campechano in Santa Cruz Atoyac.
google_maps_query: Mariscos del Diego, Santa Cruz Atoyac, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Mi Gusto Es
description: Time Out calls it the most Sinaloan marisquería on its aguachile list, serving a traditional aguachile verde. OpenTable reviewers praise the freshness and the soft-shell crab tacos. Some find the indoor mariachi loud.
special_quality: A traditional green aguachile and soft-shell crab tacos in Narvarte.
google_maps_query: Mi Gusto Es, Narvarte, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Aguachile en la CDMX

name: La Corriente Cevichería Nais
description: A livelier, newer Roma spot with seafood tacos, aguachiles, burritos and tostadas. Chilango flags the tiradito and the jurel chicharrón tostada.
special_quality: Jurel chicharrón tostada and tiradito in a casual Roma room.
google_maps_query: La Corriente Cevichería Nais, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Micheviche
description: A Hipódromo Condesa seafood bar with nine ceviches that can be turned into tostadas. Chilango points to the tostada verde of shrimp, octopus and fish. Served alongside micheladas.
special_quality: A ceviche bar built around nine ceviches that double as tostadas.
google_maps_query: Micheviche, Condesa, Ciudad de Mexico

name: Tostadas Amatista
description: A fonda-style place in Del Carmen with homestyle toppings: octopus a la gallega, tuna and bacalao. Chilango recommends the set lunch menu.
special_quality: Octopus a la gallega and bacalao tostadas with a fonda comida corrida.
google_maps_query: Tostadas Amatista, Coyoacán, Ciudad de Mexico

name: La Morenita (Mercado Medellín)
description: The best-known seafood spot in Mercado Medellín, founded more than three decades ago by Miguel Gardono. A busy, reliable stop with scallops, cocktails, huachinango a la veracruzana and paella.
special_quality: A 30-year-old market seafood counter in Roma Sur's Mercado Medellín.
google_maps_query: La Morenita, Mercado Medellín, Roma Sur, Ciudad de Mexico

name: La Nueva Viga (pasillo marisquero)
subcategory: Wholesale fish market with eating stalls
description: The fish and seafood market inside the Central de Abasto, opened in 1993 with more than 500 stalls. It is often called the second-largest in the world after Tsukiji, though that ranking comes from one outlet. Chilango points to a seafood corridor of stalls serving pescadillas, empanadas and cocteles. The old Viga site now holds seafood buffets.
special_quality: One of the world's largest fish markets, with a corridor of cook-to-order stalls.
address: Área Federal Central de Abastos s/n, Iztapalapa
google_maps_query: La Nueva Viga, Central de Abasto, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: El Financiero - Historia del Mercado de La Viga

name: The Bob Marlin
description: Chef Ricardo Rendón's restaurant brings Culiacán-style Sinaloan seafood to Hipódromo, beyond the usual aguachiles and fish tacos. Chilango lists dishes such as Double Play, Taco Don Chayo and Perfect Game.
special_quality: Culiacán-style Sinaloan seafood, with baseball-named dishes.
google_maps_query: The Bob Marlin, Hipódromo, Ciudad de Mexico

name: El Pescadito
description: Serves Sonoran-style fried seafood tacos of marlin, shrimp or fish on double tortillas, with a large stand of salsas, mayonnaises and vegetables. Time Out highlights the Quesotote, a shrimp and cheese chile relleno taco.
special_quality: Sonoran fried marlin and shrimp tacos with a self-serve salsa bar.
address: Condesa (exact street address not confirmed in sources)
google_maps_query: El Pescadito, Condesa, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Tacos de mariscos

name: Soda Fishlab
description: Time Out picks it for tacos built around smoke and cheese: the Norteño with smoked shrimp, onion, chipotle and cheese, Rompeolas with shrimp in a Manchego crust, and Bailarín with smoked marlin.
special_quality: Cheesy, smoky shrimp and marlin tacos, with a crusted-cheese shrimp.
address: Colonia Independencia (exact street address not confirmed in sources)
google_maps_query: Soda Fishlab, Independencia, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Tacos de mariscos

name: Playa Sabino
description: A family-friendly seafood spot that Time Out recommends for its buchón fish taco: battered with beer, on a handmade tortilla, with cabbage and chipotle dressing.
special_quality: A beer-battered buchón fish taco on handmade tortillas.
address: Santa María la Ribera (exact street address not confirmed in sources)
google_maps_query: Playa Sabino, Santa María la Ribera, Ciudad de Mexico

source_links.title: Time Out México - Tacos de mariscos

name: Cocina Conchita
description: Known for a crisp, light batter on its Ensenada-style shrimp taco. Time Out calls the taco essential and also praises the spicy shrimp aguachile.
special_quality: A light-battered Ensenada-style shrimp taco.
address: Roma (exact street address not confirmed in sources)
google_maps_query: Cocina Conchita, Roma, Ciudad de Mexico
